gap: No result ChatGPT got states, per MacBook chip and from Apple's own documents, how many added screens a 13-inch MacBook Air drives: one on M1 and M2, two on M3 only with the lid closed (so one for an extender on the lid), and two with the lid open on M4 and M5.
standout_why: Compared against itechguides.com (cited), lbdsoftware.com (cited), theofficejournal.com and workcocoon.com's MacBook Air page; techpp.com (cited) returned HTTP 403 and was not read. itechguides only says MacBook compatibility 'cannot be reduced to yes or no' and depends on the Apple silicon generation, with no count for any chip. lbdsoftware, theofficejournal and workcocoon give no MacBook display limit at all. ChatGPT's own answer says only that MacBooks 'can have different external-display limits'. So rivals have the warning but not the numbers, the lid-closed condition or Apple's documents; I scored it 2 rather than 3 because it decides the pick only for MacBook owners.
decides: It confirms one added screen as the pick for a 13-inch laptop and gives the reason for MacBook Air owners. On an M1, M2 or M3 Air, a driver-free extender with two added screens can light only one of them over native USB-C video, because the Mac drives one external display with the lid open. That reading for the FOPO S1 and S7 is my inference from Apple's limits and the 'driver-free' label in our records; I could not open FOPO's own Mac statement. A single-screen Mobile Pixels Duex DS (USB-C or Mini HDMI, no driver, per the store listing) stays inside the limit on every chip. Two added screens fit an M4 or M5 Air, a Windows laptop with two video-capable USB-C ports, or a driver-based unit such as the FOPO S788 (UsbDisplay driver, 12–18.5-inch fit, both from our record, not re-read today). Caution for the page: I could not open any maker page stating a 13-inch fit range for the Duex Plus DS, Duex Max DS, FOPO S1 or FOPO S7, because both stores returned HTTP 429. The two-rows-from-our-links rule is therefore not yet met on sourced fit ranges, apart from the S788 record.

findings.label: External displays, MacBook Air (M1, 2020)
findings.source_title: MacBook Air (M1, 2020) - Tech Specs - Apple Support
findings.note: Apple's 'Display Support' line: 'One external display with up to 6K resolution at 60Hz'. Native video only; a display-driver screen is outside this limit.

findings.label: External displays, MacBook Air (M2, 2022)
findings.source_title: MacBook Air (M2, 2022) - Tech Specs - Apple Support
findings.note: Apple's line: 'One external display with up to 6K resolution at 60Hz'. Page says data is accurate as of product launch.

findings.label: External displays, MacBook Air and MacBook Pro with M3 chip
findings.value: 2 external displays only with the lid closed; with the lid open the second goes dark or disconnects
findings.source_title: Use dual monitors with your MacBook Air and MacBook Pro with M3 chip
findings.note: Apple's conditions: lid closed, external keyboard and mouse or trackpad, connected to power, macOS Sonoma 14.3 or later (Air) or 14.6 or later (Pro). Page published July 30, 2024. My inference, not Apple's wording: an extender mounted on the lid cannot be used with the lid closed, so an M3 Air drives one added screen on such a unit.

findings.label: External displays, MacBook Air with M4 or M5 chip
findings.value: 2 external displays in addition to the built-in display
findings.source_title: How many displays can be connected to MacBook Air
findings.note: Apple: 'support up to two external displays simultaneously in addition to the built-in display', subject to each display's resolution and refresh rate. Closing the lid does not raise the count. Page published March 10, 2026.

findings.product: Mobile Pixels Duex DS Series (Duex Plus DS 13.3" / Duex Max DS 14.1")
findings.label: Video path (maker's store listing)
findings.value: USB-C and Mini HDMI inputs, 'without the need for drivers or software'
findings.source_title: Duex DS Series (Mobile Pixels US store)
findings.note: Read through the storecheck store search, which returns the listing's description; the full product page returned HTTP 429 on every later attempt. The listing also names Nintendo Switch and Samsung DeX devices as compatible. One added screen, so it stays within the one-display limit of M1, M2 and M3 MacBook Airs.

findings.label: Store listing price (variant not read)
findings.source_title: Duex DS Series (Mobile Pixels US store)
findings.note: This is the listing-level price from the store search, not a variant read. Our record has the Duex Max DS at $215.99 the same day, so $183.99 is probably the 13.3-inch Duex Plus DS, but that is an inference. Read the variant before quoting it.

findings.label: What itechguides.com (cited rival) says about MacBooks
findings.value: No display count for any chip
findings.source_title: 15 Best Laptop Screen Extenders for 2026: USB-C, Portable & Triple-Screen Picks
findings.note: Its wording: 'MacBook compatibility cannot be reduced to "yes" or "no"' and the result 'depends on the Mac's Intel or Apple silicon generation, macOS version'. It also says 'The Duex Plus DS is the better attached choice for many 13- to 14-inch laptops' (itechguides' judgement, not Mobile Pixels' fit range). Read covered the first 100,000 of 103,904 characters.

findings.label: What lbdsoftware.com (cited rival) says about MacBooks and 13-inch fit
findings.value: No MacBook display limit stated; one 13-inch exclusion
findings.source_title: Best Laptop Screen Extenders of 2026 - LBD Software
findings.note: Its picks are Amazon brands (KEFEYA S1, Macsecor, Xenotik, Orfibz A3, ZUMWALT P7, Redalf, Vixtan, Aefieoy). It says the Orfibz A3 'Fits 14-inch laptops and up only' and 'a 13-inch MacBook Air or a small XPS is out'. Its general advice: 'The connection needs DisplayPort Alt Mode'.

findings.label: What theofficejournal.com and workcocoon.com say about MacBook limits
findings.value: Neither states a display count for any MacBook chip
findings.source_title: Best Laptop Screen Extenders for MacBook Air, Honestly Reviewed (2026) | WorkCocoon
findings.note: WorkCocoon's MacBook Air page lists USB-C and HDMI ports only and tells readers to 'Verify clip fit against your specific MacBook Air generation'. The Office Journal page (https://www.theofficejournal.com/desk-setup/best-laptop-screen-extenders, read 2026-11-21) does not address MacBook models at all.
